title: Parky's at Moorestown Mall back on track as lawsuit ends | Exclusive - NewsBreak
text:
By Joseph P. Smith ,
11 hours ago A payment dispute that threatened the completion of a proposed family entertainment center at the Moorestown Mall has been resolved under an out-of-court settlement.
Construction started last year on Parky’s Moorestown with NACOM Companies Inc. of Runnemede as the construction firm and hopes to open the center in 2026. The project entails the conversion of a former Taylor and Lord department store.
Florida-based businessman Aaron Parkinson, a principal in the project, said in an email on July 7 that a lawsuit brought by NACOM was resolved.
More: How South Jersey celebrated the 1976 bicentennial | Exclusive
“Construction is progressing well, and we're excited about the project,” Parkinson wrote. “We'll announce a more specific opening timeline once we're confident it's finalized.”
Attorney Benjamin Sprang, who represented NACOM, said a stipulation of dismissal was filed July 7 with the court. The case was still in the evidence discovery stage.
“I can confirm that the lawsuit has been resolved,” Sprang said. “The parties have amicably resolved it.”
On Dec. 12, NACOM had filed a construction lien against property owner Parky’s FEC Holdings LLC. It claimed overdue payments for work that had been completed and billed.
The lien filing with the Burlington County Clerk’s Office was a legal prerequisite to filing an actual lawsuit if the parties didn't settle.
According to the lien filing, NACOM had been paid approximately $1.55 million for work completed as of mid-October 2025. Another $500,795 still was due and was not forthcoming on schedule, NACOM claimed.
Negotiations didn't progress, and on March 18 NACOM filed a lawsuit in Burlington County Superior Court demanding payment. Parky’s FEC was named among four defendant companies associated with the project.
The lawsuit stated that NACOM, including interest, was now owed more than $750,000.
More: Moorestown Mall entertainment center in dispute with builder
“If you do cover the project, we'd also like the community to know how much we appreciate the support we've received from Moorestown Township, the Township Council, the Planning Board, and everyone else who has helped move the project forward,” Parkinson said in his email. “We're looking forward to bringing something special to the community.”
The center is planned with two stories and approximately 121,000 square feet.
The property is located at 400 New Jersey Route 38 here.
Joe Smith is a N.E. Philly native transplanted to South Jersey almost four decades ago, concentrating on housing, politics, real estate, business, and development. He is a former editor and current senior staff writer for The Daily Journal in Vineland, Courier-Post in Cherry Hill, and the Burlington County Times.
